title: Backend Architecture
summary: I design and operate a 240-module Python backend — FastAPI and asyncio, running as production systemd services on Ubuntu — with a REST API surface of 54 route modules feeding a live operations dashboard.
fullDescription: My core engineering work is a large, real production backend: 240 Python modules built on FastAPI and asyncio, running as hardened systemd services on Ubuntu Linux. It exposes a 54-module REST API that powers a live React operations dashboard.

It's built around a proper shared-service architecture — a central engine registry, an app-state singleton, a governance and kill-switch layer, and a self-healing watchdog with heartbeats. Async background workers run on independent timers: market scans every few minutes, neural inference hourly, and scheduled briefings. I also write the specs behind it: PRDs, API surface docs, and deployment maps.
responsibilities: 240-module Python backend (FastAPI + asyncio) as production systemd services on Ubuntu
54 REST route modules serving a live React operations dashboard
Async background worker loops on independent timers (market scans, hourly neural inference, briefings)
Shared-service architecture: engine registry, app-state singleton, governance/kill-switch layer, self-healing watchdog with heartbeats
Third-party API integration with rate-limit handling (exchange data, market-intelligence feeds)
Technical specs, PRDs, API surface docs, and deployment maps

title: React Dashboards
summary: I build and maintain a React operations dashboard with real-time data panels — command center, analytics, regime performance, and alerts.
fullDescription: On the front end I build and maintain a React dashboard that serves as the control surface for my backend systems. It's organized into real-time panels — a command center, analytics views, regime-performance tracking, and an alerts feed — all driven live by the REST API behind it.
responsibilities: React dashboard with real-time data panels
Command center, analytics, regime-performance, and alerts views
Wired directly to a live REST backend

title: Self-Managed Operations
summary: I run my own production stack end to end on Linux servers I administer directly — SSH hardening, nginx, systemd, live incident diagnosis, and a disciplined Git/GitHub deploy workflow.
fullDescription: I own my infrastructure top to bottom. That means real Linux server administration: SSH hardening, user management, file permissions, systemd, and journald log management, with nginx configured as a reverse proxy in front of my services.

I deploy, restart, and monitor production services and diagnose live incidents when they happen. My Git/GitHub workflow is deliberate — a dev/main branch strategy, deploy keys with scoped access, and I've migrated a live codebase to a fresh repository cleanly. I also drive AI-assisted development directly from the terminal (Claude Code / Codex).
responsibilities: Linux server administration: SSH hardening, user management, file permissions, systemd, journald logs
nginx configured as a reverse proxy
Deploy, restart, and monitor production services; diagnose live incidents
Git/GitHub: dev/main branch strategy, scoped deploy keys, live codebase migration to a fresh repo
AI-assisted development workflows (Claude Code / Codex) in the terminal

title: Pipelines & Databases
summary: I operate MongoDB at scale (~900k documents) and build real-time ingestion pipelines — including streaming and scoring Level 2 order-book data across exchanges.
fullDescription: I run MongoDB at real scale — around 900,000 documents — handling schema design, retention planning, and query and aggregation work.

Feeding it, I build real-time ingestion pipelines and scheduled data jobs across several sources: market data, research papers, and on-chain data. That includes streaming and scoring Level 2 order-book data across multiple exchanges in real time.
responsibilities: MongoDB at scale (~900k documents): schema design, retention planning, queries and aggregations
Real-time ingestion pipelines and scheduled data jobs (market data, research papers, on-chain data)
Streaming and scoring Level 2 order-book data across exchanges

title: Quantitative Research
summary: I enjoy working with markets. I do market-structure and derivatives analysis, run a strategy lab with 64,000+ evaluations, and turn raw data into plain-English briefings.
fullDescription: I like understanding how markets are put together. I do market-structure analysis — support/resistance mapping, order-book imbalance, liquidity walls, and multi-timeframe bias scoring across crypto assets — plus derivatives intelligence like funding rates, open interest, and positioning proxies.

On the quantitative side I've run a strategy lab with 64,000+ evaluations, with backtesting frameworks and performance metrics (win rate, Sharpe-style scoring, regime analysis). The end goal I care about most is the 'understanding layer': translating raw market data into plain-English briefings, and auditing research claims against live databases so papers get reconciled with actual evidence.
responsibilities: Market-structure analysis: support/resistance, order-book imbalance, liquidity walls, multi-timeframe bias scoring
Quantitative strategy research: a strategy lab with 64,000+ evaluations, backtesting, win rate / Sharpe-style scoring, regime analysis
Derivatives intelligence: funding rates, open interest, positioning proxies
Research synthesis: raw market data into plain-English briefings
Auditing research claims against live databases and reconciling papers with evidence

title: Operations & People Management
summary: Co-owner and operator of a family landscaping business, and I've run my own event-parking venture. I know how to lead a team, keep clients happy, and manage the money.
fullDescription: Alongside the engineering, I'm a co-owner and operator of my family's landscaping company — which is really a crash course in running a real business. I handle day-to-day operations: scheduling, crew management, client relations, equipment, and route planning, plus the full financial side — billing, payroll, bookkeeping, budgeting, and financial management.

I've also run my own venture: an event-parking business for Formula 1 weekend, where I set pricing strategy, managed online listings, and handled the logistics of operating a 12-acre lot. Together these are the practical skills that don't show up in code — leading people, managing money, and making the operational calls that keep a business running.
responsibilities: Team & people management: leading and scheduling a crew
Client relations and customer communication
Financial management: billing, payroll, bookkeeping, budgeting
Operations & logistics: equipment, route planning, day-to-day coordination
Ran an F1-weekend event-parking venture: pricing strategy, online listings, logistics for a 12-acre lot
